Subject: HealthSync pilot — prompt outputs storage mapping & retention asks

Thanks again for the call earlier today — great to hear more about the triage workflow you want to pilot. As promised, quick post-call summary focused on how Redwood will handle prompt inputs and generated outputs during the pilot: 

- What we store: ephemeral request logs (headers, timestamp, model id), prompt text by default only when required for debugging or quality monitoring, generated outputs when explicitly configured to persist (e.g., for historical triage and human-in-the-loop review).
- Where it lives: hosted pilot in our US region; logs + persisted outputs live in encrypted object storage in us-west with separate access controls.
- Default retention (pilot): request logs 30 days; persisted outputs 90 days. We can shorten or extend per contract.
- Access controls: RBAC for Redwood Console, role-based lm-access for your team, and optional KMS-backed keying for output storage.

Attached is a simple mapping workbook (healthsync-data-map.xlsx) that maps HealthSync data flows to Redwood storage locations. Can you confirm which data elements you will mark as "must not persist" vs "ok to persist" for the pilot? That will let us set up sanitization rules and reduce storage at day 0.

Next steps I propose: 
1) HealthSync to mark required persistence for three example flows (triage-search, symptom-normalization, automated-summaries) — reply here with the attached workbook updated.
2) Redwood to provide a formal retention & encryption addendum (we can include a short clause in the SOW).
3) Security Q&A exchange (SOC2 evidence + KMS configuration) — earliest availability: next Wed if that works.

Thanks — I copied Neha (security & compliance) and Ben (solutions) to help scope the technical updates.

—Monica

Hi Monica — thanks for the clear recap. A couple of clarifying questions before we update the workbook: 

1) When you say "prompt text by default only when required for debugging or quality monitoring" — does that mean prompt text is stored anywhere for the pilot unless we explicitly opt out? We need to know the opt-out mechanism and whether sanitization (PII redaction) can be applied before persistence.

2) Are generated outputs treated differently from prompts in terms of retention and search indexing? For our triage use case, we would like outputs retained for 180 days but with strict role-bound access (only product ops + clinical reviewers).

3) Where are the audit logs stored and for how long? Our auditors will want an immutable trail showing who accessed persisted outputs and when.

4) Can you confirm whether Redwood supports customer-managed keys (KMS) for data at rest for the pilot or if that's only available on Private deployments?

We can return the workbook back to you by EOD tomorrow once we align internally.

Thanks,
Rajiv

Subject: Re: HealthSync pilot — prompt outputs storage mapping & retention asks

Hi Rajiv — quick answers inline below. I'm copying Ben for implementation notes.

1) Prompt persistence: by default, prompt text is not persisted long-term. For the hosted pilot we keep short-term request traces (30 days) which include non-persistent prompt text only when you've toggled "persist_prompts" for a specific route in the Console or explicitly opted in via API flag. We will provide a per-route "persist_prompts" boolean and the default will be false. Sanitization: we offer server-side redaction rules (regex + named-field scrubbing) that can run before persistence; those run as a pre-write hook and can be applied to any route.

2) Outputs: persisted outputs are stored separately from logs and are indexed only if you opt into the "searchable outputs" feature. Retention is configurable per-output-store; for pilots we can set 180 days for the triage store as requested and limit search access. We will map product ops + clinical-review role to a Console role with explicit read privileges.

3) Audit logs: access logs and read events are written to an immutable append-only store (S3 with object lock + separate write-only ingestion). Default access-log retention is 1 year; we can export a filtered view (CSV or Splunk/Datadog stream) on request. If you need a longer retention for compliance, we can add an export hook to your SIEM.

4) KMS: customer-managed keys are supported on Redwood Private deployments and also available for Dedicated/Tenant setups with an enterprise add-on. For the hosted pilot we can offer envelope encryption using our KMS; if you require full CMK control we should discuss Private or Dedicated options in the SOW.

I'll add these details to the attached summary PDF and push it to the Drive link.

—Neha

Neha/Monica — thanks for the quick responses. A few follow-ups from our InfoSec team before we sign the SOW: 

- Can you provide an example audit extract (sanitized) showing read events for a persisted output and the related Console role mapping? We don't need PII in the example, just the event shape and retention metadata.
- For server-side sanitization, do redaction rules run synchronously before persistence (blocking) or asynchronously? We need guarantees that no raw PII will be written to the persisted output store if a rule matches.
- Are persisted outputs versioned and do you offer an append-only history for outputs that have been corrected/annotated by clinicians?

Also please include the relevant SOC2 test ID references in the exported evidence (if possible) so our auditors can cross-check.

—Priya on behalf of HealthSync Security

All — thanks for the feedback and the questions. Quick commitments and proposed next steps so we can move to SOW: 

Commitments:
- Example audit extract: we will provide a sanitized CSV extract (no PII) showing read/access event shape, Console role mapping, and retention timestamps by EOD Thursday.
- Sanitization behavior: redaction rules are configured as pre-write hooks and run synchronously; if a rule matches, the raw field is never persisted to the output store. We will document this behavior in the SOW appendix and include a small test harness for you to validate.
- Versioning: persisted outputs are versioned (object-level metadata) and we can enable an append-only history for clinician annotations; retention applies per-version.

Action items: 
1) HealthSync: please update the attached workbook with the three flows and mark persistence choices (expected by 2027-09-22).
2) Redwood: we'll deliver the sanitized audit extract + updated retention addendum (SOW appendix) by 2027-09-23.
3) Optional: if CMK is a hard requirement, let's schedule a short call to scope Private/Dedicated pricing (Ben to follow up).

I'll upload the materials to the Drive link and post a HubSpot note against the deal (HS-2027-09-14-01). If you prefer a one-pager instead of the workbook updates we can accept that as the mapping.

Thanks — looking forward to the pilot.

—Monica
